newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends mostly lower ahead of GCA data.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends mostly lower ahead of GCA data.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures erased sharp early gains to finish mainly lower on Tuesday, as speculators led a late sell-off in anticipation of build in U.S. stockpiles, dealers said.
"The specs were liquidating near the close because it's scary to be long if you are expecting a big increase in stocks," said Victor Henriquez, president of Hencorp Becstone in Miami.

While most industry sources expected the monthly Green Coffee Association of New York report, due after today's close, to show a 250,000 to 350,000-bag increase in U.S. warehouse stocks during March, Henriquez said projections as high as a 700,000-bag rise have swirled around the market.

Spot May delivery fell 3.60 cents per lb on the day, to 192.40 cents, after trading from 201.50 to 191.00. Second-month July settled 2.35 cents lower, at 174.65 cents, while the back months closed up 2.60 to down 2.50.
The May/July switch, a barometer of nearby availability, narrowed to 17.75 cents, up from 19.00 cents at the close on Friday.

The New York market defied pre-opening expectations and gapped some 2.00 cents higher at the outset, buoyed by news of a lower Colombian estimate and a strike at Brazil's key port of Santos. Upward momentum accelerated after the May contract triggered buy-stops above 199.00 cents.

After Monday's close, the chief of Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation, Jorge Cardenas, said that the counrtry's output totalled 10 million 60-kg bags in 1996/97 (April-March), down from about 14 million in the same 1995/96 period.
Cardenas also said production between April and September was seen at about 4.5 million bags.

In Brazil, stevedores at the port of Santos began a strike on Tuesday for indefinite period, bring loading and unloading of ships to a halt, a union official said. The official said that the strike could spread to a national level on Wednesday.
Additionally, traders noted that Colombian truck drivers are set to go on strike starting Sunday, April 20.
"Come Monday morning, if we see Colombia and Brazil on strike, I think we'll see new highs," one trader said.
Technically, traders pegged May support at 190.00 cents, then 187.00 cents. May's next upside objective was seen at 205.00 cents.
